six-towns.title: Six development towns combined, 2019–2022: how these towns voted
six-towns.question: Share of valid votes cast inside Sderot, Netivot, Ofakim, Beit She'an, Kiryat Shmona and Dimona together, computed from the Central Elections Committee's per-locality result files for the 21st–25th Knessets.
six-towns.note: Files for each election at media21–media25.bechirot.gov.il/files/expc.csv. Lists are named as they ran that year. Otzma Yehudit ran inside the Union of Right-Wing Parties (with Jewish Home and National Union) in April 2019, alone in September 2019 and March 2020, and inside the Religious Zionism joint list (with Noam) in 2021 and 2022, so that row is a different list each time. National Unity, a separate list in 2022, took a further 4.0% in the six towns. Soldiers' and other double-envelope votes are not assigned to any locality

towns-2022.title: Each town, 2022 (and Likud in 2020): how these towns voted
towns-2022.question: Share of valid votes cast in each locality, computed from the Central Elections Committee's per-locality result files for the 23rd (March 2020) and 25th (November 2022) Knessets.
towns-2022.note: 2020 file at media23.bechirot.gov.il/files/expc.csv. Religious Zionism 2022 was the joint list of Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit and Noam. Netivot and Ofakim have large Haredi populations, so their Shas and UTJ shares are not a traditional vote

draft-deal.title: Suspending the "Military Service Exemption Law" called "a political deal," by religiosity
draft-deal.question: Asked about the government's decision "to suspend the Military Service Exemption Law and to transfer billions of shekels to Haredi institutions," share choosing "A political deal that prioritizes sectoral interests over the good of the public."
draft-deal.source: Israel Democracy Institute, Israeli Voice Index
draft-deal.note: The other main answer, "a responsible decision": Haredi 51%, national religious 34%, traditional religious 43%, traditional non-religious 25%, secular 8%
